body:
Google just published a holiday shopping guide built on search data, not guesses.

Most small businesses read that as "big brand news" and move on. The distinction that matters: it's not about ad budgets, it's about timing — when people start searching before they buy.

Here's the mechanic worth knowing. Google tracks search interest by category and publishes when it peaks, weeks before the actual buying date. If you sell anything seasonal, that peak is when your ad or your Google Business Profile needs to already be live, not when you finally get around to it.

Most small accounts do the opposite. They start campaigns the week they feel ready, not the week their customer starts looking. By the time the ad goes live, the searcher has already bought from whoever showed up first.

This costs nothing to check. Go to Google Trends, type your product category, and look at the last two years. The search spike repeats on roughly the same week every year.

What week does your category's search interest actually spike, and is your account live before it or during it?
